title: Research: rank-8 masked decoders are gauge-rigid on every P108 unit — 168 orbit certificates, census-free coverage (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p108/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

#1419's extension lemma makes P112 minus X rigid whenever X lies inside a frame of P112. For four-line punctures that leaves **168 of the 180 FRAME0-stabiliser orbits**, 6132952 of 6210820 quadruples: 166 orbits contain an odd pair and 2 are orthogonal but lie in no P112 frame. This PR proves rigidity on all 168 with #1425's per-unit method. Each representative gets:

- a pivot passing #1212's (I3) and (I4) with gluing, with 16 to 24 complete classes;
- #1399's Lemma 9 for the other 4–36 lines;
- a new DRUP refutation of the zero-pattern CNF for (I2), of 1373 to 3168 lemmas and 361027 in total.

**New: coverage without a census.** The verifier does not enumerate the 6.2 million quadruples:

- Every quadruple contains a triple, and the 24 triple orbits are cheap. So every quadruple is equivalent to a *candidate*, a triple-orbit representative plus one line. There are 2517 candidates.
- 49 candidates lie inside a P112 frame, which is #1419's case; that property is invariant, because the group fixes FRAME0.
- For each of the other 2468, `COVER.json` gives a word in the generators, of length at most 10, that carries a unit's quadruple onto it. `verify.py` replays every word.

**Consequence.** With #1419, **every P108 unit** (P112 minus any four lines) is rigid. Every decoder with exactly eight costly terms in the E-graph model there has cst ≥ 60, which is #968's 72 − p at p = 12.

This is the follow-up to #1469 (P109) mentioned there. The two packages are independent, since neither uses the other.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p108/verify.py` runs 174 exact checks in about 2.5 minutes, standard library only:
  - **Self-contained.** It has its own E8 model, triple orbits, cover-word replay, pivot conditions, CNF builder and two-watched-literal RUP checker. It replays all 168 proofs from `PROOFS.json.gz` (about 6 MB), and the SHA256 of each decompressed proof and each CNF is pinned.
  - **Controls.** The gauge pattern satisfies each CNF. Each proof fails without the "some entry vanishes" clause. An empty-clause-only proof is rejected.
- **Cross-check, run once:** an independently written census (OpenAI Codex, from a specification only) finds the same 180 quadruple orbits. It has 12 inside a P112 frame (77868, matching #1419's census) and 168 open, 2 of them orthogonal. The coverage argument does not need it.
- **AI review:** a read-only adversarial review, also by Codex, checked the coverage argument and the P108 edge cases (classes with a single live row). It found no soundness gap. Its one wording point, that `verify.py` does not prove the 168 units lie in distinct orbits, is applied: the PASS line says "168 rigid units cover every P108 quadruple outside a P112 frame", and distinctness is credited to the census. This is not a human review.
- `make_proof.py` (python-sat 1.9.dev15 with Glucose 4.1, plus numpy and scipy) regenerates `UNITS.json`, `COVER.json` and `PROOFS.json.gz` byte-identically in about 40 s. numpy only proposes the orbit grouping; the verifier checks every word.
- Passes on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14. `scripts/research_package.py`: the metadata check and the Python 3.12 registered replay pass. `test_research_*` passes.

## Not checked or not covered

- **Inherited steps**, cited and not re-derived:
  - #1212's Lemmas 5–6, §7 and transport;
  - #1399's Lemma 9;
  - #1419's Lemma 10 and its P104 inputs, for frame-contained quadruples.

  All of these PRs are open. #968's (F6) is inherited. Attainment of 60 is not checked. There has been no independent human review.
- **P107 to P105** are the open next question. Per-orbit certificates already take about 6 MB here, and P105 has on the order of 10⁵ orbits, so going deeper needs a structural replacement for the DRUP step (I2).
- **Nine or more costly terms.**

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** `complex-masked-decoder` (scope key `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`), refined to #1469's open next question. Track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 2. The task was assigned by the donor as "the open thread".
- **Heads:** base `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`. Cites #1212 `57099cb5`, #1399 `4e1ba3a1`, #1419 `81b8997b` and #1425 `4b707c22`. It imports nothing from them.
- **Claim:** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1411#discussioncomment-18912490 (P109; updated for P108 in the same thread).
- **Overlap:** none beyond my own claim and #1469. Refreshed at 01:20Z (819 open PRs and 166 discussions, complete pagination).

- **DreamingOfClouds (#717):** the E-graph model.
